s_datadir_hint: SQLite cache: keep on appdata, not the flash
s_ignore_unmanaged_desc: Skip containers not created from an Unraid template (Docker Compose, Dockhand, plain docker run). Only Unraid-managed containers stay in ShipLog.
s_updates_sub: What happens when you click "Update now" in a changelog bubble. ShipLog stays read-only: it triggers Unraid's own update either way.
s_confirm_desc: Show a confirmation prompt before the update starts. Off = one click updates straight away.
s_silent_desc: Run the update without Unraid's pop-up window and its download log. The update still runs in the background.
s_registry_sub: Optional: both raise rate limits so ShipLog can read versions & changelogs for more of your containers. Leave empty to stay anonymous.
s_gh_hint: Reads release notes from GitHub. Anonymous GitHub allows only ~60 requests/hour. With many containers that runs out fast and changelogs come back empty. A classic Personal Access Token (no scopes needed) raises it to ~5000/hour.
s_dh_hint: Checks the newest version + digest of docker.io images. Anonymous Docker Hub is rate-limited per IP. With many images that throttles, so those show an update without a version number. A free Docker Hub access token (read-only) lifts the limit. Username + token, both required.
s_ai_sub: Optional: a model condenses each changelog into "what changes / breaking / risk", locally through Ollama or llama-swap, or through OpenRouter.
s_ollama_url_hint: Probes common local Ollama ports and fills this in.
s_notif_sub: Optional: a message on the channels below when a new update is first seen. An update that auto-update will apply appears in its run summary instead, unless it is critical.
d_unmaintainedHint: No more updates. Consider migrating to a maintained alternative.
d_updateHint: triggers Unraid's own update for this container
d_updateGone: Couldn't find Unraid's update button. Use 'apply update' on the row.
d_confirmAll: Update all %n containers with a pending update now?
d_updateAllHint: triggers Unraid's own update for every container with a pending update
d_none: No changelog text found for this image. Open the repo (top-right) for the release notes.
d_noSource: This image names no source repository, so ShipLog has no release notes to show. If the project keeps them on GitHub or in a changelog file, set that under "source" in its row on ShipLog's status page.
d_unraidStale: Unraid still shows an update here, but this container already runs the newest image of its tag (checked %d). Unraid's display is out of date: click Check for Updates at the bottom of the Docker tab to clear it.
d_rateLimited: GitHub's hourly rate limit was reached, so the release notes couldn't load. Add a GitHub token in ShipLog's settings (Sources) to raise it.
s_ca_warn: CA Auto Update is also installed. Both will update containers, so use only one to avoid double updates.
s_au_enable_desc: Apply container updates automatically on the schedule below, up to the level you choose. Off by default.
s_au_level_desc: Auto-apply only updates at or below this level. Patch = bug fixes; Minor = new features; Major = may break. Unknown (non-versioned) tags are never auto-updated.
s_au_exclude_desc: Comma-separated words. Blocks an otherwise-eligible update whose changelog text contains any of them (case-insensitive), e.g. "breaking" catches a release that calls out a breaking change even at a minor or patch bump. Blocked updates are reported, never applied. Empty = off.
s_au_digest_desc: Containers on a rolling tag like :latest carry no version level. Turn this on to auto-apply their digest updates too.
s_au_sched_desc: When to run. Daily runs once at the time you set; At boot runs once after the array is up; Every N hours/days runs on that interval.
s_au_dryrun_desc: Don't apply anything, just send a notification of what WOULD be updated. Use this first to see the plan before arming real updates.
s_llamaswap_url_hint: Works with any OpenAI-compatible server, such as llama-swap, LM Studio or vLLM. When set, ShipLog uses it instead of Ollama.
s_au_containers_desc: Choose which containers auto-update may update. Switch one off and ShipLog never updates it on its own, so you update it by hand. Manual updates, changelogs and risk badges stay as they are. Click Apply to save.
s_au_ct_off: Auto-update is off. Turn it on above to pick containers.
s_au_ct_none: No containers yet. The first scan may still be running.
d_autoHintOff: Left out of ShipLog's scheduled auto-update. Updating it by hand still works.
d_autoFailed: Couldn't save. Reload the page and try again.
d_autoOffBadgeHint: Left out of ShipLog's scheduled auto-update. Click to change.
d_wobHintOn: Updates even if the backup app couldn't back it up first.
d_wobHintOff: Updates only after the backup app has backed it up.
d_heldNote: ShipLog held back the last auto-update because the backup didn't finish: %s
d_rolledNote: The last auto-update failed (%s), so ShipLog put the container back on its old image. Your appdata is untouched.
d_rolledUnpin: Its template now points at the old image. To update again, remove the @sha256 part from the repository.
s_au_pinned_desc: A container pinned to a version tag (for example :1.4.2) is never auto-updated, because pulling the same tag again changes nothing. A newer version only shows up as a hint; change the tag yourself to update.
d_newerChipHint: Newer version %v available. The tag is pinned, so change it to update.
d_newerNote: Version %v is available. Change the tag to update.
d_newerWhy: This container is pinned to %v, so pulling it again changes nothing and ShipLog never auto-updates it.
s_session: the session has expired, reload the page
s_vc_hint: The version of {app}, where its updates stand and what this version brought.
s_cc_hint: Everything {app} is made of or brings along, with its version.
s_help_body: Problems, wishes or suggestions? You're welcome to open an issue on GitHub, or come say hi on Discord.
s_about_body: ShipLog is a free plugin for Unraid's Docker tab, built by one knight on evenings and weekends, with no accounts, no telemetry and no ads.
s_about_coin: If it has earned a place on your server, toss a coin to your knight: it helps cover the costs and keeps the project alive.
s_give_appeal: Toss a coin to your knight: it covers part of the costs and keeps the project alive. Everything I build costs nothing and shows no ads.
s_give_coffee_intro: The payment runs through Buy Me a Coffee. You do not need an account.
s_give_paypal_intro: The payment runs through PayPal, with your PayPal account or by card without one.
s_give_thanks: Thank you, your donation went through.
s_give_failed: PayPal cannot be reached right now. Try again later or pick another way to give.
s_give_crypto_intro: Pick a currency and a network, then scan the code or copy the address.
s_give_no_tag: No destination tag and no memo needed.
s_fortress_no_backup: Until then, auto-updates run without a backup.
s_vulns_sub: ShipLog can look up the packages of each running image in an open vulnerability database. The Docker tab then shows a badge with the known critical and high vulnerabilities next to the container, and the changelog window lists them along with how many the newest image closes. An update that closes a critical one moves its risk badge up a step.
s_vuln_check_desc: On by default. ShipLog takes each image's package list from its registry, or from the package database inside the container when the image has none, and sends only package names and versions to the open vulnerability database at api.osv.dev. Container names, image names, tags and everything else about your server stay with you. Results are cached, so the check costs a few small requests a day. Turning it off saves the little memory and traffic it uses.
d_vulnBadgeHint: Known critical and high vulnerabilities in this container's image. Click for details.
d_vulnRunning: Known vulnerabilities in the running image: %v.
d_vulnNone: The running image has no known critical or high vulnerabilities.
d_vulnCloses: The newest image closes %v of them.
d_vulnClosesNone: The newest image still has all of them.
d_vulnNewestUnknown: The newest image comes without a package list, so ShipLog can't tell what the update closes.
d_vulnSystem: ShipLog could only check the system packages inside the container.
d_vulnNoPackages: ShipLog couldn't read a package list for this image, so it can't say which vulnerabilities it has.
d_vulnFailed: The vulnerability database couldn't be reached. ShipLog tries again at the next check.
d_vulnInstalled: Known vulnerabilities in the installed image: %v.
d_vulnNoneInstalled: The installed image has no known critical or high vulnerabilities.
d_vulnRaised: Rated a step higher: the update closes %v.
d_reason_minor: minor version bump %1 → %2 (new features, review the changelog)
d_reason_patch: patch version bump %1 → %2 (fixes only, low risk)
d_reason_pinned_newer: pinned to %1, newer version %2 available, change the tag to update
d_reason_breaking_in: breaking change flagged in %1 release notes ("%2"), review before updating
d_reason_breaking: breaking change flagged in the release notes ("%1"), review before updating
d_reason_digest_pinned: pinned by digest, updates only when the pin changes
d_reason_local: no registry digest (built or loaded locally), not checked against a registry
d_reason_image_id: referenced by image ID, no tag to compare
d_vulnNoUpdate: No update fixes these yet, because they are in the image the publisher builds. You can ask the project for a fixed image, or switch to another tag or image.
d_vulnBoth: %f with a fix available, %u with no fix yet
s_notify_hub: TollRoll sends ShipLog's notifications while it is the fortress's hub. The channels below take over again as soon as it stops.
nc_add_hint: Pick where messages go. A service can be added more than once, say for two Discord channels.
nc_name_hint: Shown above the channel and in the log when a message does not get through.
nc_token_hint: Leave it empty when the address already carries one.
nc_body_hint: Sent as written. %%title%%, %%body%%, %%ok%%, %%time%% and %%link%% are filled in for each message.
nc_smtp_hint: Sends each message as a plain-text email through your mail server.
nc_smtp_to_hint: Several addresses are separated by commas.
nc_apprise_hint: Posts to an Apprise API server you run yourself, which passes the message on to every service its key is set up for.
nc_apprise_urls_hint: Such as tgram://... or pover://..., separated by spaces. With these, the address above is the server's /notify without a key.
nc_apprise_tags_hint: Only the services with one of these tags get the message. Empty sends to all of them.
nc_matrix_hint: Posts into a room as the account the access token belongs to. That account has to be in the room.
nc_discord_hint: Posts each message to a Discord channel through its webhook address.
nc_slack_hint: Posts each message to a Slack channel through an incoming webhook.
nc_ntfy_hint: Publishes each message to an ntfy topic. Failures arrive with high priority.
nc_gotify_hint: Sends each message to your Gotify server. Failures arrive with a higher priority.
nc_webhook_hint: Sends each message to an address of your choice, with the method, headers and body you set.
nc_hc_hint: Pings a check when a run starts and again when it ends, so a run that never happens shows up as a missed ping. A held job counts as failed there.
nc_fail_invalid: Something is missing, or an address is not one.
nc_fail_moved: The saved secret belongs to the address it was saved with. Type it again.
nc_fail_dns: The server's name could not be found.
nc_fail_auth: The server did not accept the token or the login.
nc_fail_not_found: The server knows no such address.
nc_fail_redirect: The server sent the message on to another address, which is not followed.
nc_fail_rejected: The server turned the message down.
nc_fail_rate_limited: The server asks to wait before the next message.
nc_fail_server: The server ran into an error.
nc_fail_no_starttls: The mail server offers no STARTTLS.
nc_none: Nothing matches “{query}”. A webhook reaches almost any service.
nc_unraid_hint: Shows each message in Unraid's own notifications. Unraid passes it on to every agent you set up there.
nc_empty: No channel yet. Add one, and the messages reach you wherever you are.
nc_headers_hint: One per line, as Name: value.
s_or_notice: With OpenRouter, every summary sends the changelog text, the image name and the running and new version to openrouter.ai, which passes them to the provider of the model you pick. Container names, settings and everything else about your server stay here. While Local is chosen, nothing goes to OpenRouter.
s_or_model_hint: Pick a model from OpenRouter's list or type its ID.
s_or_key_hint: Make a key just for ShipLog. It stays on the flash drive, where only root can read it, and goes to openrouter.ai alone. This page shows no more of it than its last four characters.
s_or_check_hint: Asks OpenRouter whether it accepts the key and lists the model. Nothing is generated, so the check costs nothing.
s_or_try_hint: Has the model summarize a short sample changelog. This is a real request and uses a few hundred tokens.
s_or_err_invalid_key: OpenRouter does not accept this key
s_or_err_no_credit: The key has no credit left
s_or_err_model_unavailable: This model is not available on OpenRouter right now
s_or_err_rate_limited: OpenRouter is limiting requests. Try again in a minute.
s_or_err_bad_answer: The model answered, but ShipLog cannot read the answer as a summary. Try another model.
s_or_err_failed: OpenRouter could not handle the request. The details are in /var/log/shiplog.log.
s_or_err_bad_key: That does not look like a key
s_or_err_save_failed: The key could not be saved
